objective: Resolve all six TASK-006 review findings by making hook failures encoding-safe and strengthening the UTF-8 regression suite without changing the established file-encoding behavior.
requirements: Make stop_guard.py fail closed when implementation.md or context.jsonl cannot be decoded or read, returning exit code 2 with a diagnostic on stderr instead of allowing an unhandled exit 1.
Make session_start.py handle unreadable UTF-8 inputs without crashing, report omitted input on stderr, and continue injecting any remaining readable context.
Emit SessionStart output as explicit UTF-8 bytes so Japanese and other non-cp1252 text reaches stdout on Windows without UnicodeEncodeError.
Strengthen the two misleading JSON round-trip tests and the tautological ASCII test in place so each assertion accurately describes and detects the behavior it claims to cover.
Add mutation-sensitive coverage proving removal of a required encoding argument is detected rather than relying on tests that pass because json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True.
Correct the AST audit so positional binary modes in open(path, 'rb') and os.fdopen(fd, 'rb') are excluded while text-mode calls remain audited.
Avoid repeatedly reading and parsing the same scoped source files across AST audit tests.
Preserve the existing explicit UTF-8 encoding arguments and all behavior outside the six findings.

files_to_modify.purpose: Catch decode and read failures for guard inputs and convert them into an explanatory fail-closed exit code 2.
Handle unreadable inputs explicitly and emit injected context through a UTF-8-safe stdout path.
Strengthen the ineffective encoding and ASCII assertions, add mutation-sensitive audit coverage, fix binary-mode classification, and cache parsed audit results.

files_to_create.purpose: Provide isolated subprocess regression tests for malformed hook inputs, fail-closed exit behavior, diagnostic output, and non-cp1252 SessionStart injection.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Malformed UTF-8 in either worker-writable Stop guard input produces exit code 2 and an explanatory stderr message, while valid completed write-back behavior remains allowed.
SessionStart emits Japanese text as UTF-8 without raising, reports unreadable input while exiting successfully, and remains quiet when no task is active.
The UTF-8 audit detects an encoding argument removed from real scoped source, and the strengthened round-trip and ASCII tests assert their actual byte-level invariants.
The AST audit classifies open(path, 'rb'), os.fdopen(fd, 'rb'), Path.open binary modes, and keyword binary modes as binary while continuing to flag text open calls without encoding.
The complete non-empty unittest suite passes under Python 3.9 and Python 3.12.

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
A Stop guard read failure must return exit code 2 with a reason and must never escape as exit code 1.
SessionStart is an injector rather than a blocker, so unreadable input must be reported and omitted without returning exit code 2.
Do not weaken or delete existing tests; strengthen F4 and F5 coverage in place and preserve useful JSON-escaping behavior under accurate assertions.
Keep the explicit UTF-8 file encoding behavior introduced in the four TASK-006 production files exactly as established; this task changes failure handling, output emission, and tests around it.
Do not address platform-dependent newline translation, _support.py text I/O, diff-scope base selection, or unrelated attribute calls named open.
Declare workflow hook changes explicitly as required by the constitution and ADR-0004.
risks: Writing through sys.stdout.buffer can conflict with replaced or captured text streams that lack a buffer, so the output helper needs a safe fallback without reintroducing locale-dependent failure.
Catching decode failures too broadly could hide programming errors; handling should be limited to expected UnicodeDecodeError and filesystem read failures with visible diagnostics.
A permissive SessionStart fallback could silently lose blackboard content, so tests must assert both successful continuation and the stderr warning.
Scanning all positional string arguments for binary modes could misclassify unusual calls; tests should cover supported open, Path.open, and os.fdopen forms plus a text-mode counterexample.
Caching AST results can make deliberately mutated test inputs stale if keyed incorrectly; source-based mutation checks should bypass or isolate the path cache.
The Python launcher and both requested interpreter versions must be installed in the validation environment for the dual-version acceptance command to run.
test_strategy: Run hook scripts as subprocesses from isolated temporary repository-shaped directories, using raw malformed bytes and clearing Python stdout encoding overrides so Windows locale failures are not masked.
Test malformed implementation notes and context JSONL independently, asserting exact blocking or degrading exit contracts and useful stderr diagnostics.
Inject Japanese context and inspect captured raw stdout for its UTF-8 byte sequence, alongside ASCII and no-task regressions.
Exercise AST audit logic directly on synthetic binary and text call forms and on an in-memory mutated copy of real scoped source.
Retain and strengthen JSON escaping, Unicode round-trip, ASCII compatibility, and ADR tests while ensuring their names and assertions match the behavior they actually prove.
Run focused test classes first, then execute full unittest discovery under Python 3.9 and Python 3.12.
